title: Fuel — Tail Trim Tank — Transfer Valve and Forward Return Line Rework, VANTOR
abstract: Replacement of the tail trim tank transfer valve by a unit with a higher-ratio actuator and an integral heater mat, and re-routing of the forward return line to shorten the transfer response at top of descent.

sections.planning_reason: Flight data monitoring at three operators showed the aft transfer valve taking up to eleven seconds to reach the commanded position against a design figure of four, which delays the forward transfer at top of descent and leaves the aircraft trimmed further aft than the schedule intends. Nine crew reports of a late forward transfer message were recorded in two years. The actuator gearbox wears faster than predicted, aggravated by the long cold soak the tail tank sees on the ultra-long sectors these aircraft fly. The tail trim tank exists only on the four-engine aircraft.
sections.description: The transfer valve sub-assembly is replaced by a valve with a higher-ratio actuator gearbox and an integral heater mat rated for continuous operation below minus 40 degrees Celsius. The forward return line is re-routed to reduce the number of bends between the tank outlet and the wing junction, and the upper non-return valve is moved 300 mm forward on the new route.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Put the aircraft on jacks and de-fuel the trim tank. WARNING: DO NOT OPEN THE STABILIZER ACCESS PANELS UNTIL THE TANK IS PURGED AND THE ATMOSPHERE TEST IS RECORDED. Get access through the stabilizer access panels in zones 331 and 341 and through the wing junction in zone 613. Remove the transfer valve sub-assembly D2820133531277 and cap the lines. Install the left-hand transfer valve KA206956-14 with the heater mat and connect the mat to the existing tank heating bus. Remove the forward return line and install the re-routed line from the kit, closing each joint with solid rivets AGS247313K4 at the support brackets and plain washers LN213180-50 under the clamps. Move the upper non-return valve position 14QT 300 mm forward onto the new route. Re-calibrate the upper transmitter position 40QT to the revised line length. Do AMM-S-28-20-13-700-013-A as the transfer functional test, including a timed valve response measurement at ambient and at minus 30 degrees Celsius simulated. Close the tank, do the leak check and lower the aircraft. Record the embodiment and the revised empty mass.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to all VTR-64C3 and VTR-68R2 aircraft. There is no production cut-in because both four-engine lines are closed, so the whole population is pre-modification. The twin-engine aircraft have no tail trim tank and this Service Bulletin does not apply to them in any configuration.
sections.material_note: Kit K2820-1034-01 contains the transfer valve, the re-routed line, the brackets and the fastener set. It is built against firm order only because the population is small; lead time is thirty-four weeks from order. The removed valve is returned for teardown.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled C-check where the aircraft is on jacks, or within 48 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.
